rules.title: Aggregate return types are returned by value
rules.statement: A function whose return type is a tuple, struct, ZonedStruct, or payload-carrying (tagged) enum returns the aggregate by value (as a value of the aggregate's storage type), never as a pointer to function-local storage; this guarantees the returned value outlives the callee frame.

rules.title: Payload-free enum returns as i32
rules.statement: A function returning a C-style enum (an enum with no payload variants, so no tagged-enum layout) returns its discriminant as a 32-bit integer rather than an aggregate.

rules.title: Reference-kind return ABI determined by RefRepr descriptor
rules.statement: When the return type is a reference kind, its by-value return representation is the reference's RefRepr: dyn-trait and slice references return their 16-byte fat (pointer,metadata) pair by value; closure / custom-DST / thin references return their 8-byte value pointer.

rules.title: AnyVal is represented as a 32-bit value
rules.statement: A value of type AnyVal is represented as a 32-bit integer in both parameter and return position.
rules.uncertainty: i32 likely encodes a handle/index into an AnyVal table; exact semantics inferred from representation only.

rules.title: Array parameters are passed by pointer
rules.statement: A parameter whose type is an array [T; N] is passed by pointer (to the array storage), not by value.

rules.title: Variadic functions are extern-only C-ABI declarations
rules.statement: A function declared variadic (vararg) is emitted only as an external declaration through the LLVM-dialect function op (`llvm.func`, `isVarArg=true`, external linkage) — the `func` dialect used for ordinary Logos functions has no vararg support — and is a declaration only in this path, with no Logos-level body generated for it.
rules.uncertainty: This unit shows only the vararg lowering path (llvm.func extern-style declaration, no body); whether a non-extern fn with a vararg parameter is rejected elsewhere (sema) is not visible in this slice.

rules.title: Each mangled function symbol must have at most one body
rules.statement: Two distinct functions resolving to the same mangled link symbol is an error; in particular a private function in one package and a pub function of the same base name in an imported package must not collide, requiring rename to disambiguate.

rules.title: Methods are emitted under module-qualified link symbols
rules.statement: A function's emitted link symbol is its module-qualified name: methods gain the module prefix; free functions and extern functions keep their bare name. Symbol identity and forward-declaration deduplication key off this link name, while Logos-level parameter-type/coercion maps used at call sites are recorded under BOTH the qualified link name and the bare name (call sites may reference the bare name during body emission).

rules.title: Void function body may fall through to an implicit return
rules.statement: A function with no return type (void) whose body reaches the end of its final block without an explicit terminator gets a plain `return` with no operand inserted implicitly.

rules.title: Sema-accepted exhaustive non-void tail lowers to `unreachable`, not a return
rules.statement: For a non-void function whose body falls through to the end of codegen without an explicit terminator (e.g. an exhaustive tuple/struct `match` with no wildcard arm — a path sema's reachability analysis has already accepted as complete, but which mlir-gen's dispatch lowering does not itself prove exhaustive), mlir-gen inserts an `unreachable` terminator instead of a value-producing return, so the function still verifies structurally; this path is dead code, never executed at runtime.

rules.title: A by-value tagged-enum parameter is one heap-pointer level
rules.statement: A by-value function parameter of a tagged (payload-carrying) enum type (e.g. `Option<i64>`) arrives at the callee as a single heap-pointer level (the boxed enum), not the aggregate itself and not a pointer-to-pointer; taking its address (`&x`) spills that pointer into a local slot to produce a genuine pointer-to-enum-pointer, as required by two-level-pointer enum methods (e.g. `==`). A payload-free (C-style) enum parameter is instead a plain i32 and takes the scalar-spill address-of path.
rules.uncertainty: The underlying enum-boxing/representation decision (why tagged enums are one heap-pointer level as a value) is established by code outside this slice; this unit only consumes and documents the resulting parameter-binding convention.

rules.title: Arrays of structs store elements inline, not as pointers
rules.statement: An array type `[Struct; N]` — including when reached through a reference/pointer parameter, which peels to the array's element type before indexing — lays out its elements inline and contiguously (each element occupies exactly the struct's full layout size), rather than storing a pointer per element; indexing strides by that element layout size, not by the size of a pointer.

rules.title: Slice references are a {data-pointer, length} fat descriptor
rules.statement: A `&[T]` / `&mut [T]` reference parameter arrives as a pointer to a fat descriptor pair `{data: *T, len}`; indexed element access dereferences the descriptor's data-pointer field first, then applies the element's layout stride (using the element's full struct layout when the element type is itself a struct, so struct-typed slice elements are laid out inline within the pointed-to buffer).

rules.title: Writing through a pointer derived from a shared reference to a Freeze pointee is undefined
rules.statement: Let `r: &T` be a shared reference whose pointee type `T` is Freeze (no `UnsafeCell` is reachable through T's own inline bytes — struct fields, enum payloads, tuple and array elements, NOT across an indirection). Then for the whole lifetime of `r` the referent is IMMUTABLE, and any write through a pointer whose provenance chain is rooted at `r` is undefined behaviour. This holds regardless of how the pointer was obtained: `r as *const T as *mut T`, `NonNull::from_ref(r)`, a reborrow, a field projection, or any chain of these. The rule is about the PROGRAM, not about any optimisation: a program that performs such a write has no defined meaning, whatever the compiler emits. EXCEPTION — LOADED POINTERS ARE NOT DERIVED. If a pointer-typed VALUE is read out of the referent and written through, the write carries that loaded pointer's OWN provenance, not `r`'s, and is defined. The write must not land in the referent's own bytes; it lands in whatever the loaded pointer addresses. This exception is what makes `Rc` and `Arc` sound and is not optional: `Rc<T> { inner: *mut RcInner<T> }` is Freeze precisely because the indirection stops the Freeze recursion, so `&Rc<T>` does carry the immutability guarantee, while `Rc::clone` increments a refcount reached by LOADING `self.inner`. Without the exception this rule would condemn `Rc::clone`, `Arc::clone`, `Weak::upgrade` and `Rc`/`Arc::downgrade`, all of which are correct today. COMPOSITION: the write itself already requires an `unsafe` context (see `stmt.deref-write.raw-ptr-unsafe`), so no SAFE program can reach this rule; the obligation binds exactly where an obligation already sits. This matches Rust, where the same rule is what licenses `noalias`+`readonly` on a shared reference — it is NOT a divergence.
rules.uncertainty: UNTESTABLE IS A CLASSIFICATION, NOT AN EXCUSE. No Logos program's pass/fail can decide whether an undefined-behaviour rule holds, so the prohibition has no conformance test by construction. What IS mechanized is everything the rule licenses: tests/logos/ir/param_attrs_freeze pins the emission on definitions, param_attrs_freeze_declare pins it on the (far larger) imported-declaration surface, and param_attrs_freeze_lattice pins the Freeze predicate's arms ONE PER VERDICT SITE — a population DERIVED from the predicate by tests/logos/freeze_arm_coverage.py rather than listed, because the five axes it started with left twelve of seventeen verdicts unpinned and deleting the TUPLE arm's element recursion was MEASURED to hand `&(Cell<i64>, i64)` a noalias+readonly with all five of them green. Among those arms, `axis_ptr_field` is the mechanical guard on the EXCEPTION clause: it fails the moment the Freeze recursion stops stopping at an indirection, which is the one change that would make Rc/Arc non-Freeze and the exception moot. tests/logos/ir/param_attrs_freeze_interior pins the INTERIOR-MUTABILITY POPULATION against the emitted IR — the stdlib types the predicate must answer FALSE for, derived over all of stdlib rather than read out of one file. The prose of the rule is held against the code by tests/logos/shared_ref_ub_lint.sh, which hashes each delimited `@claim` block in the emission site: checking that a rule-id STRING is present was measured to pass a comment whose every clause had been reversed.
